title: Abs
summary: The rectus abdominis, the 'six-pack' muscle from the breastbone to the pubic bone. It curls the ribcage toward the pelvis and resists the spine being arched. Loaded crunches, leg raises done with a pelvic curl, and rollouts train it.

what_it_is.overview: The app's abs region is the rectus abdominis only; the obliques and serratus are a separate group. The 'six-pack' lines are tendon bands across one muscle, not separate muscles.

heads.name: Rectus abdominis
heads.origin: The top of the pubic bone at the front of the pelvis.
heads.insertion: The bottom of the breastbone and the cartilage of the fifth to seventh ribs.
heads.fiber_direction: Vertical, running straight up the front of the belly, crossed by three or four tendon bands.

what_it_does.action: Spinal flexion (curling the ribcage toward the pelvis).
what_it_does.detail: The job in crunches and cable crunches.

what_it_does.action: Posterior pelvic tilt (curling the pelvis toward the ribs).
what_it_does.detail: What makes a leg raise an ab exercise instead of only a hip-flexor exercise.
The job in rollouts, planks and hollow holds.

what_it_does.action: Helps brace the trunk with the obliques and deeper abdominal muscles.
what_it_does.detail: Part of how the trunk stiffens under heavy squats and deadlifts.

synergists.name: Obliques
synergists.role: Help flex and brace the trunk.

synergists.name: Hip flexors
synergists.role: Lift the legs in leg raises; not tracked.

antagonists.name: Lower back (erector spinae)
antagonists.role: Extends the spine, the opposite of a crunch.

stabilizer_roles.text: In squats, deadlifts and overhead presses the abs brace isometrically; the library rates most of these below 0.25 for abs, so they add no ab sets.
Rollouts and front levers load the abs at long length against arching; ab-wheel rollouts are rated 1.0.

relationships.indirect_note: Each working set adds the exercise's rating for this muscle to the weekly total, and ratings under 0.25 count as 0. 3 sets of cable crunch (1.0), 3 sets of hanging leg raise (1.0) and 3 sets of cable woodchop (0.4) give 3 + 3 + 1.2 = 7.2, which the panel shows as 7 (rounded to the nearest 0.5). The full list comes live from exercises.json; the rows above are examples and the ratings are coaching estimates.

how.joint_angle: Curl the ribcage down toward the pelvis; the hips stay still.
how.stretch_position: Let the spine extend at the top of a cable crunch.
how.stance: Kneeling at a cable or seated in a machine.

bias.caveat: Load can be added in small steps, like any other muscle.

bias.goal: Leg raises that hit the abs

how.joint_angle: Lift the legs, then curl the pelvis up at the top.

bias.caveat: Without the pelvic curl, the hip flexors do most of the lift.

how.joint_angle: Roll out until the body is long, without letting the low back sag.

bias.caveat: Rollouts are hard where the abs are long. A stretch-growth benefit for abs is not tested.

how.joint_angle: Crunches move the ribcage; reverse crunches and leg raises move the pelvis.

bias.caveat: It is one muscle. Coaches use both styles for variety; separate upper or lower growth is a model.

best_exercises.why: Loadable spinal flexion with cable tension.
Guided crunch with easy load steps.
Free-weight crunch through a long range.
Pelvis-to-ribs curl; abs 1.0, obliques 0.5, needs grip.
Anti-extension at long length; abs 1.0, obliques 0.6.
Standing variation for those who dislike kneeling.

mistakes.text: Pulling with the arms or hips on cable crunches instead of curling the spine.
Swinging leg raises with no pelvic curl, so the hip flexors do the work.
Letting the low back sag at the end of a rollout.
Doing endless light reps; abs respond to hard sets like other muscles.

coach_cues.why: Turns a leg raise into an ab exercise.

coach_cues.cue: Squeeze your glutes and keep your ribs down on rollouts.
coach_cues.why: Keeps the lower back from arching.

notes: Weekly target in the app: 4 to 16 abs sets at Advanced. Intermediate and Beginner scale the minimum by 0.8 and 0.6; the maximum stays the same. Render the numbers from targets.json, not from this text.
No ab growth study by exercise choice is on file, so nothing here is marked supported.
Visible abs depend mostly on body fat; this page is about training the muscle only.
